Properties that can be measured include local crystallographic orientations, orientation gradients and strains. arxiv-2208-07954.title: Surface roughness noise analysis and comprehensive noise effects on depth-dependent coherence time of NV centers in diamond
arxiv-2208-07954.creator: P. Chrostoski †,∗, P. Kehayias ‡, D. H. Santamore ∗
arxiv-2208-07954.description: Abstract Noise is a detrimental issue for nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, causing line broadening and decreasing the coherence time ( T 2 T_{2} ). Following our previous electric and magnetic field noise work, we investigate noise caused by the diamond surface roughness, which is a source for charge density fluctuations and incoherent photon scattering.

arxiv-2209-13293.creator: Hanamichi Kawamura
arxiv-2209-13293.description: Abstract . In this paper, we introduce iterated integrals associated with colored rooted trees and give proofs for the shuffle relations for 𝒑 \boldsymbol{p} -adic finite and t t -adic symmetric polylogarithms. arxiv-2212-08796.description: Abstract . Text password has served as the most popular method for user authentication so far, and is not likely to be totally replaced in foreseeable future. Password authentication offers several desirable properties (e.g., low-cost, highly available, easy-to-implement, reusable). However, it suffers from a critical security issue mainly caused by the inability to memorize complicated strings of humans.

arxiv-2307-02425.title: Geometric control of tilt transition dynamics in single-clamped thermalized elastic sheets
arxiv-2307-02425.creator: Roberto Abril Valenzuela, Paul Z. Hanakata, Mark J. Bowick
arxiv-2307-02425.description: Abstract We study the finite-temperature dynamics of thin elastic sheets in a single-clamped cantilever configuration. This system is known to exhibit a tilt transition at which the preferred mean plane of the sheet shifts from horizontal to a plane above or below the horizontal. The resultant thermally roughened two-state (up/down) system possesses rich dynamics on multiple time-scales.

arxiv-2403-03025.title: Predictive power of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless theory based on Renormalization Group throughout the BCS-BEC crossover in 2D superconductors
arxiv-2403-03025.creator: Giovanni Midei, Koichiro Furutani, Luca Salasnich, Andrea Perali
arxiv-2403-03025.description: Abstract Recent experiments on 2D superconductors allow the characterization of the critical temperature and of the phase diagram across the BCS-BEC crossover as a function of density. We obtain from these experiments the microscopic parameters of the superconducting state at low temperatures by the BCS mean-field approach.

arxiv-2412-13109.title: Time-Biased Random Walks and Robustness of Expanders

arxiv-2412-13109.description: Abstract Random walks on expanders play a crucial role in Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithms, derandomization, graph theory, and distributed computing. A desirable property is that they are rapidly mixing, which is equivalent to having a spectral gap γ \gamma (asymptotically) bounded away from 0 0 . Our work has two main strands.

arxiv-2502-06901.title: Enabling Autoregressive Models to Fill In Masked Tokens
arxiv-2502-06901.creator: Daniel Israel, Aditya Grover, Guy Van den Broeck
arxiv-2502-06901.description: Abstract Historically, LLMs have been trained using either autoregressive (AR) or masked language modeling (MLM) objectives, with AR models gaining dominance in recent years. However, AR models are inherently incapable of masked infilling, which is the ability to predict masked tokens between past and future context.

arxiv-2504-10733.title: Cross-Problem Parameter Transfer in Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm: A Machine Learning Approach
arxiv-2504-10733.creator: Kien X. Nguyen, Bao Bach, Ilya Safro
arxiv-2504-10733.description: Abstract Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is one of the most promising candidates to achieve the quantum advantage in solving combinatorial optimization problems. The process of finding a good set of variational parameters in the QAOA circuit has proven to be challenging due to multiple factors, such as barren plateaus.

arxiv-2507-18499.title: The hidden subgroup problem for infinite groups
arxiv-2507-18499.creator: Greg Kuperberg
arxiv-2507-18499.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Greg Kuperberg. Dedicated to Eleanor Rieffel, my friend and colleague for 42 years and counting. Following the example of Shor’s algorithm for period-finding in the integers, we explore the hidden subgroup problem (HSP) for discrete infinite groups. On the hardness side, we show that HSP is 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard for the additive group of rational numbers, and for normal subgroups of non-abelian free groups.

arxiv-2601-15141.title: CLEANER: Self-Purified Trajectories Boost Agentic Reinforcement Learning

arxiv-2601-15141.description: Abstract Agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) has empowered Large Language Models (LLMs) to utilize tools like Python interpreters for complex problem-solving. pmc-10695467.description: Background: Pseudotumor cerebri (PTC) or idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is characterized by elevated intracranial pressure without hydrocephalus or mass lesion, with normal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) studies and neuroimaging. The exact cause remains uncertain, but potential mechanisms include increased CSF production, impaired CSF absorption, cerebral edema, and abnormal cerebral venous pressure gradients.

pmc-11462822.title: Serum lncRNA ITGB2-AS1 and ICAM-1 as novel biomarkers for rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis diagnosis
pmc-11462822.creator: Aliaa M Selim, Yumn A Elsabagh, Maha M El-Sawalhi, Nabila A Ismail, Mahmoud A Senousy
pmc-11462822.description: BackgroundThe complete circulating long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) signature of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA) is still uncovered. The lncRNA integrin subunit beta 2 (ITGB2)-anti-sense RNA 1 (ITGB2-AS1) affects ITGB2 expression; however, there is a gap in knowledge regarding its expression and clinical usefulness in RA and OA.

pmc-11478461.creator: Adam Stech, Patrik Kamencay, Robert Hudec
pmc-11478461.description: The increasing demand for accurate and detailed 3D modeling in fields such as cultural heritage preservation, industrial inspection, and scientific research necessitates advanced techniques to enhance model quality. This paper addresses this necessity by incorporating spectral imaging data to improve the surface detail and reflectivity of 3D models.

The key component of this environment is decentralized identity management (DIM), embracing an identity and access management strategy that empowers computing devices and individuals to manage their digital personas. Aggregation operators (AOs) are valuable techniques that facilitate combining and summarizing a finite set of imprecise data.

pmc-12581515.description: Extracranial metastasis of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma is very rare and poorly understood at the molecular level. We report a case of FGFR3::TACC3 fusion IDH-wildtype glioblastoma in a 61-year-old male, whose preoperative blood sample showed highly aberrant cfDNA fragmentation patterns, which could be suggestive of early systemic dissemination, undetected by standard-of-care imaging of his body.

pmc-12626867.title: Advancements in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer therapy: from molecular profiling to the advent of precision oncology
pmc-12626867.creator: Chen Yang, Yanchi Shao, Yu Zhang, Huan Zhang, Yanbin Zhao
pmc-12626867.description: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is challenging to manage due to its high malignancy and early metastatic spread. Although initial chemoradiotherapy responses are common, resistance rapidly develops, and long-term efficacy remains limited. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) overcome previous survival barriers, extending overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in extensive-stage SCLC. Nevertheless, absolute clinical benefits remain modest.

pmc-12647772.title: Optimization of compact fractal monopole antenna with partial fractal ground using machine learning approach for multiband applications
pmc-12647772.creator: Guntamukkala Yaminisasi, Pokkunuri Pardhasaradhi, Satti Sudha Mohan Reddy, Kokku Aruna Kumari, Om Prakash Kumar, Ishwar Bhiradi, B T P Madhav
pmc-12647772.description: In this research, we investigate the integration of machine learning techniques, in particular Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) and Support Vector Regression (SVR), into the optimization of compact microstrip antenna design. Multiband operation with a significant miniaturization is achieved by proposing a unique circular radiating structure with decorative slots and a central star shaped patch.

pmc-12659296.title: The patterns and determinants of healthcare utilisation of older adults in rural Odisha, India – a cross-sectional study
pmc-12659296.creator: Mohanasundaram Mourougan, Arvind Kumar Singh, Abhisek Mishra, Binod Kumar Behera, Binod Kumar Patro
pmc-12659296.description: BackgroundIndia’s population is ageing rapidly, with an estimate that one in every five Indians will be 60 years or older by 2050. Ageing with the ongoing epidemiological transition increases the burden on already strained healthcare systems of the country. Older adults face health related, financial and social vulnerabilities including access to healthcare facilities, especially in rural areas.

pmc-12956821.title: Humans 40,000 y ago developed a system of conventional signs
pmc-12956821.creator: Christian Bentz, Ewa Dutkiewicz
pmc-12956821.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SignificanceHumans have carved visual signs into the surfaces of mobile artifacts and cave walls since several hundred thousand years. We here analyze a 40,000 y old assemblage of mobile artifacts bearing sequences of intentionally engraved geometric signs. These sign sequences have a complexity comparable to the earliest protocuneiform and were selectively applied to yield higher information density on figurines than on tools.

pmc-13027445.title: Eccentric Isokinetic Rehabilitation for Chronic Lateral Epicondylitis in Female Swimmers: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Bilateral Neuromuscular Adaptations and Functional Performance
pmc-13027445.creator: Wissem Dhahbi, Hatem Ghouili, Halil İbrahim Ceylan, Nessrine Adhadhi, Souhail Bchini, Manel Bessifi, Nagihan Burçak Ceylan, Valentina Stefanica, Nejmeddine Ouerghi, Nadhir Hammami

Materials and Methods: Twenty-five swimmers (age 46.1 ± 3.1 years) with lateral epicondylitis exceeding three months’ duration completed a randomized controlled trial comparing eccentric training in Controlled Active Motion mode (experimental group (EG), n = 13) against passive motion in Continuous Passive Motion mode (control group (CG), n = 12).
